channel.title: MFA Insights
channel.description: Practical tax, accounting, and QuickBooks guidance for individuals and small and mid-sized businesses: IRS, New Jersey and New York filing deadlines and tax updates, tax planning, accrual accounting, bookkeeping best practices, and QuickBooks tips.

item.title: ANCHOR Deadline 2026: NJ Property Tax Relief Is Due Nov. 2
item.description: The ANCHOR deadline for 2026 is Nov. 2. One PAS-1 form covers ANCHOR, Stay NJ (up to $6,500) and Senior Freeze. Who qualifies, amounts and who must file.

item.title: 2027 Tax Calendar: Key IRS, New Jersey and New York Tax Deadlines
item.description: The 2027 tax calendar: every key IRS deadline plus New Jersey and New York due dates, from 1099s and W-2s to April 15 and estimated taxes. Save it to your calendar.

item.title: Year-End Tax Planning 2026: 4 Dates That Can Still Lower Your Tax Bill
item.description: Year-end tax planning 2026 in four dates: Oct. 15, Dec. 31, Jan. 15 and April 15. What to do by each one, with 2026 IRA, HSA and 401(k) limits.

item.title: Federal Scholarship Tax Credit 2027: The New $1,700 Credit Explained
item.description: The federal scholarship tax credit starts Jan. 1, 2027: up to $1,700 per person for cash gifts to approved scholarship groups. Who qualifies, which states, and NJ.

item.title: Section 179 vs. Bonus Depreciation for 2026: Year-End Equipment Guide
item.description: Section 179 deduction 2026 limit is $2.56M and 100% bonus depreciation is back. How to write off equipment by Dec. 31, which to use, and the NJ catch.

item.title: Form 1099 Preparation Guide for 2026 Payments: The New $2,000 Rule and How to File Right
item.description: The 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC threshold jumps to $2,000 for 2026 payments. Who needs a 1099, the 2027 deadlines, and a step-by-step QuickBooks process to file right.

item.title: October 15, 2026 Tax Extension Deadline: What to Do Before It Hits
item.description: Filed an extension for your 2025 return? Your deadline is Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026. What to file, what waiting costs, and the NJ and disaster-area exceptions.
